previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of mitochondrial myopathy, coronary artery disease, and orthostatic hypotension was admitted for evaluation of intermittent chest pressure over two days, associated with nausea and diaphoresis. Initial concerns for acute coronary syndrome were raised due to his cardiac history, but serial troponins were negative and EKG showed only transient ST depressions. A chest x-ray revealed no acute process, and an exercise stress echocardiogram showed normal left ventricular function with no evidence of inducible ischemia. His symptoms were attributed to dehydration, exacerbated by his mitochondrial disease, which also caused a transient rise in creatinine from baseline. He was treated with 2 liters of IV normal saline, restarted on clopidogrel after a 5-day hold, and continued on his baseline cardiac medications. His condition improved, and he was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to maintain hydration and follow up with his primary care physician and cardiologist.
